17y4bc7:334: The article describes a "teach once, reuse countless times" Skill creation flow: the user adjusts expected behavior while having the Agent actually perform the task, and once the task is done correctly, the user says "summarize the process we just went through into a Skill," and the Agent automatically invokes the built-in skill-creator capability to generate SKILL.md. The key significance of this mechanism is shifting maintenance responsibility from the technical side (modifying prompts/code) to the business side (demonstrating correct behavior). Compared with traditional Prompt Engineering, Skills generated this way derive from behaviors the user actually demonstrated rather than described, reducing the semantic gap between expression and execution. From a system evolution perspective, when business processes change, users can update Skills by re-demonstrating rather than manually editing, lowering the maintenance barrier while making Skill evolution speed more easily synchronized with business requirement changes.

v2r17u:256: The article clearly states that Bedrock is not yet available in the AWS China regions (Beijing/Ningxia), so the solution must rely on third-party model services. This constraint in turn gave rise to the model-agnostic design in the architecture: the model layer is decoupled via baseURL + API Key, so switching providers involves only configuration changes rather than architectural changes. From a supply chain compliance perspective, keeping model provider evaluation and selection at the business level (rather than hardcoding it into the architecture) is necessary — data export compliance requirements for China-based enterprises make model provider qualification assessment a key part of procurement decisions, not an afterthought of technical selection. This design downgrades "which model to use" from an architectural decision to a configuration decision, reducing the actual cost of provider replacement.
